mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: In a sample of 20 such labor strength events, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (not available in the provided catalog) would drive equity valuations higher, but since we cannot proxy retail sales, a proxy using industrial production (INDPRO) rising by 3% month-over-month predicts similar demand dynamics and positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positively correlated with INDPRO monthly change (Pearson rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in two consecutive months suggests supply-side weakness that reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during confirmed INDPRO contraction episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.3% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to respond with a negative 20-day forward return as market anticipates rate hikes that erode equity discount rates.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly inflation > 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During such inflation spikes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a sustained rise in labor participation (PAYEMS) suggests a broadening labor market, which historically precedes equity market strength and positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS increases by >2% in the following month
failure_condition: Over 10 such labor expansion events, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coincident rise in both FEDFUNDS and HOUST (industrial production) by at least 1% in the same month indicates dual accommodative signals that drive risk-on sentiment, producing positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >=1% and HOUST increases by >=1% in the same month
regime_hint: dual accommodative policy and production signal
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies move in the same direction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained decline in UNRATE below 5% without a corresponding change in FEDFUNDS, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit positive 20-day forward returns as labor market softness reduces recession fears and supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 5% for 4 consecutive months with no increase in FEDFUNDS
regime_hint: labor market softening without policy tightening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE stays soft without FEDFUNDS response (p > 0.05).
